instruction.sound: Select the size-mometer to find out what it does.

feedback.end: Seismometers record the strength of the Earth’s shaking. They can be used by scientists to find out where an earthquake happened.

atoms.b: The Richter scale ranges from 1 to 10 and is used to measure earthquakes. Each level of ((tsunami ++earthquake)) is ten times stronger than the one before.
For example, an earthquake measuring 4 is ((++ten two)) times more powerful than one measuring 3.
The higher the level on the ((Richard ++Richter)) scale, the more destructive the earthquake.

instruction.text: Listen and select the correct description.

atoms.a: An earthquake is recorded at 9 on the Richter scale.

b.sound: The earthquake causes the ground to violently shake and buildings to come crashing down.
The earthquake creates vibrations similar to a lorry passing by.

atoms.a: Another earthquake measures 2 on the Richter scale.

b.sound: The earthquake can barely even be felt.
The earthquake causes windows to shatter.

feedback.end: An earthquake can only really be felt if it measures 3 or above on the Richter scale.

instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: In order to keep people safe from earthquakes, governments follow the 3 Ps.
Prediction involves scientists monitoring plate boundaries so action can be taken before an earthquake.

Prevention involves building earthquake resistant buildings and evacuating people before the earthquake. It is impossible to prevent an earthquake from happening, but we can prevent them from affecting so many people.
Preparation involves having emergency supplies and a plan of action that can save lives. Countries can prepare for an earthquake by ensuring that everybody knows what to do if one hits.

atoms.a: How can the damage from an earthquake be reduced?

hint.text: More than one answer can be correct.
